hero.title: What type of couple are you? The quiz to take together
hero.description: Inseparables, partners in crime, independents or builders? Fifteen everyday situations, to answer together, on the same phone, to find out which family you belong to. With, for each family, its strength and its weak spot.
hero.subtitle: Fifteen questions, three minutes, to answer together

section1.title: There isn't one right type of couple, there are four
section1.intro: People often think a happy couple looks like something specific: lots of time together, lots of laughter, plans. In real life, the couples that last don't look alike at all.
section1.p1: This quiz sorts couples into four big families. The inseparables do almost everything as a pair, and they love it. With the partners in crime, everything goes through laughter. The independents each have their own life and come back together in the evening. And the builders are heading somewhere: a flat, a child, a project.
section1.p2: None of these four ways of living as a couple is better than another. Each has its strength, and each has a weak spot you don't see because you're inside it. They're detailed just below.
section1.p3: What the quiz gives you is a name for what you are, and one thing to keep an eye on. It sounds simple, but putting a word on your way of living as a couple changes quite a few things. You understand why a certain friend thinks you never see each other anymore, or why the other one needed some air last month.

section2.title: The four types of couple
section2.sub1P1: Their strength: a security few people know. You're never alone, someone is always expecting you somewhere. Inseparables understand each other quickly, because they live the same things at the same time.
section2.sub1P2: What to keep an eye on: the lack of air. When everything is lived as a pair, there's nothing left to tell each other in the evening. And the day one of you needs an evening to themselves, the other can take it as rejection when it isn't one.
section2.sub2P1: Their strength: lightness. A bad day ends with an evening spent making fun of everything, and tensions don't settle in. These are the couples you invite to be sure the evening will go well.
section2.sub2P2: What to keep an eye on: humour as a hiding place. When a subject hurts, a joke arrives and the conversation stops. Some things need to be said without laughing, and for partners in crime, that takes a small effort.
section2.sub3P1: Their strength: nobody feels smothered. Each has their friends, their projects, sometimes their holidays, and what's shared is chosen. Independents often last a long time, precisely because the relationship doesn't weigh on them.
section2.sub3P2: What to keep an eye on: the flatmate trap. Getting along well while each leading your own life, you can end up sharing a flat more than a story. A fixed date, just the two of you, is usually enough to avoid that.
section2.sub4P1: Their strength: a direction. They know where they're going, they talk about money openly, they make plans. A couple heading somewhere gets through the flat periods better, because it has a reason to wait.
section2.sub4P2: What to keep an eye on: the emptiness after the building site. Once the flat is bought and the child is asleep, there has to be something left to say to each other. Builders do well to keep room for what serves no purpose.
section2.tip: Many couples are a mix of two families. If your top two bars are close, read both profiles: it's often the mix that describes you best.

section3.title: How to answer, and what the result says
section3.p1: You answer together, on the same phone. For each situation, four answers, one per type of couple. You pick the one that looks most like you, even if none fits perfectly. When you disagree, that's exactly where it gets interesting! Talk for two minutes, then pick the answer that describes what you actually do, not what you'd like to do.
section3.p2: The order of the answers changes with every question, so you can't answer "always the first one" without reading. At the end, you see the four bars and the profile that stands out. If no family clearly dominates, the quiz says so rather than deciding by a single vote: that's the chameleon couple, which changes with the period.
section3.p3: This quiz describes your way of living as a couple. It doesn't measure how solid your relationship is, or the way each of you loves taken separately. And if you want to know through which gestures the other feels loved, that's something else again: your partner's love language is measured with a separate test.

seo.faq1Q: What are the different types of couple?
seo.faq1A: There are as many classifications as there are books on the subject. This quiz keeps four, described above: the inseparables, the partners in crime, the independents and the builders. There's also a fifth result, the chameleon couple, for couples where no family dominates.
seo.faq2Q: Can a couple change type over time?
seo.faq2A: Yes, and it's even common. Many couples start out inseparable, become builders when the flat and the children arrive, then go back to being partners in crime or independents once the children grow up. Taking the quiz again a few years apart often gives a different result, and that's not a problem.
seo.faq3Q: We don't agree on an answer, what do we do?
seo.faq3A: You talk about it for two minutes, and you choose what happens most often at yours. If it's stuck, take the answer of the one who most often feels that things aren't like that. And make a note of the question: a disagreement about "what we are" often says more than the final result.
seo.faq4Q: Is one type of couple better than the others?
seo.faq4A: No. All four types last, and all four types split up. What counts is that the way of living as a couple suits both of you. An independent with an inseparable will have a harder time than two independents together. The problem comes from the gap between the two, not from the type.
seo.faq5A: Yes. Your answers stay on your phone, there's nothing to fill in or create, and the result appears right after the fifteenth question.
